name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social platforms, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology, alert systems, and workflows for monitoring coordinated accounts over time. This is the researcher's longest-running and most cited methodological contribution, actively extended through the vera.ai WP4 work and the 2026 VERA-AI Alert system.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation Narratives
description: Study of disinformation, misinformation, and 'fake news' as phenomena within the hybrid media system, including monitoring of disinformation narratives (war in Ukraine, LGBTQI+ rights, elections) under the PROMPT project and foundational taxonomy work on misleading information.

name: Platform Governance, APIs & Data Access
description: Research on social media platforms' data-access regimes, API changes, and regulatory frameworks (Digital Services Act, Meta's political content policies, CrowdTangle shutdown), including service as an independent expert for the European Commission's Joint Research Centre on systemic risks of VLOPs.

name: Political Polarization & Partisan Media Dynamics
description: Analysis of partisan attention, insularity, cross-partisan engagement, and polarization dynamics in news circulation on social media, spanning Italian, German, Brazilian and broader European electoral contexts.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media in Disinformation
description: Emerging focus on how generative AI tools are used to produce persuasive or deceptive content (e.g., gambling promotion, deepfakes) and to counter disinformation, reflecting current teaching (IA Generativa e Media) and 2025-2026 publications on synthetic visual persuasion and LLM-based countermeasures.

name: LLMs in Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological work validating and integrating Large Language Models into text classification, annotation, and political discourse analysis pipelines, including challenges of human-machine agreement in coding social media content.

name: Italian Electoral Communication & News Ecosystem
description: The MINE programme's core empirical line: mapping Italian news media coverage, Facebook/Instagram engagement, and coordinated networks around Italian elections (2018, 2019 European, 2022), forming the institutional backbone of the researcher's agenda.

name: Health Misinformation & Problematic Content Networks
description: Mapping coordinated networks that circulate problematic health content (COVID-19, vaccines) in Italy, India, and Nigeria, including fact-checking acceleration tools developed under MINE-FACTS and the Gates Foundation-funded project.

name: Social TV & Second-Screen Audience Engagement
description: Earlier but still-referenced research stream on Twitter-based audience participation around television programming, establishing the researcher's early computational social media methods before the pivot to disinformation studies.

name: Computational Social Science Methods & Research Ethics
description: Foundational and ongoing methodological contributions on using social media data (Facebook, Twitter) for social research, including ad-based survey recruitment, ethics of computational social science, and evaluation of embedding models for text clustering.

name: Public and Sociotechnical Approaches to AI Safety Evaluation
description: Papers framing AI safety practices—red-teaming and evaluation—as sociotechnical activities requiring public involvement, labor consideration, and participatory science methods rather than purely technical procedures.

name: Online Radicalization and Extremism Across Platforms
description: Empirical and review studies of how extremist actors (far-right, jihadist) exploit platform affordances, algorithms, and multimodal content to spread and normalize radical ideologies online.

name: Retrospective Essays on Platformization and Social Media's Trajectory
description: Reflective anniversary/position essays diagnosing the current state of social media and platform economies, tracing how platformization, political economy, and scam/extractive logics have reshaped online life over the past decade.

name: Public Attitudes and Labor Experiences with AI
description: Survey- and discourse-based studies of how publics and workers perceive, use, and are shaped by AI systems, including stakeholder discourse, national attitudes, and worker-reported productivity and displacement effects.

name: LLMs and Computational Methods for Research Workflows
description: Methodological papers deploying LLMs or fine-tuned models to augment scholarly tasks such as peer review, qualitative coding, and domain-specific classification, with attention to human-in-the-loop design and evaluation.

name: Message-Based Interventions for Climate Communication and Misinformation Resistance
description: Experimental and review studies testing how framed messages, chatbots, or inoculation techniques shape audience attitudes, resistance to misinformation, and engagement with climate or conspiracy content.

name: Survey Data Quality, Comprehension, and Recruitment
description: Papers examining the methodological foundations of online survey research, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how representative and valid different opt-in sample sources are, and how novel platform-based recruitment strategies (e.g., Facebook ads) can be used and evaluated for reaching hard-to-survey populations.

name: Computational Approaches to Social Network Structure and Community Formation
description: Papers developing or applying computational/graph-based methods to detect, map, and explain emergent structural patterns—communities, practice clusters, and transitive ties—in large-scale online social networks, using techniques such as self-supervised graph embeddings and causal network analysis.

name: Cultural Imaginaries and Framings of Generative AI
description: Papers examining how generative AI is culturally imagined, discursively framed, and theorized as a medium, ranging from newspaper coverage and Silicon Valley community discourse to media-theoretical accounts of AI's distinctive properties as a creative medium.

name: Recalibrating misinformation exposure and harms narratives
description: Papers that use empirical, large-scale, or naturalistic data to challenge alarmist public and scholarly assumptions about the prevalence, exposure patterns, and societal harms of online misinformation, showing that exposure is concentrated among few users, effects are limited, and everyday misinformation is broader and less exotic than commonly assumed.

name: Conspiracy Narratives Across Media Contexts
description: Studies examining how conspiracy theories and conspiratorial narratives are formed, represented, and circulated across different media environments—including journalism, alternative media networks, and image-centric social platforms like Instagram—focusing on the media logics and discursive strategies that shape conspiracy belief and narrative construction.

name: Performing Authenticity Under Platform Demands
description: Qualitative and mixed-methods studies examining how users negotiate authenticity, care, and legitimacy through performative practices shaped by platform affordances and demands — including micro-influencers' branding of ethical care, Reddit users' bot-like imitative posting, and TikTok influencers' normalized incivility — arguing that these practices function as culturally negotiated, platform-specific survival or participatory strategies rather than fixed properties of sincerity or malice.
